title: Logos, sharpening as you name them
what: Every logo on screen from the first frame, blurred past recognition, and each one snaps into focus as you say what it is. Nothing is drawn behind or under them: no box, no label. Each fills the same square whatever shape its file is, and the square holds the row's layout, so a logo coming into focus never shifts its neighbours.
when: Naming two or three products or tools in one breath. The words go by faster than a viewer can picture them, and the blur says how many are coming without giving away what they are. The caption is already saying the words, so a label under the mark would say them twice -- reach for chipRow instead when the things being named have no logo.

cue.cue: the phrase that puts the row on screen, blurred
cue.until: the phrase it should leave on
